title: Layerwise compressed-weight simulation and adaptive fidelity latch for int8/int4 evals
creator: Priya Patel
description: Create a faster, layerwise simulation harness that approximates the effect of int8/int4 weight compression (AWQ and GPTQ flavors) without requiring a full compile-and-serve run, and use the resulting signals to drive an adaptive fidelity latch (gate) that automatically tightens/relaxes deployment thresholds per-route and per-cohort.
background: Current quantization impact runs are expensive: full compile+serve for each profile takes hours and ties up GPU capacity. We need a lightweight simulation path that gives high-fidelity deltas for relative ranking and threshold tuning. Separately, rollout gates are static; they don't account for differing cohort sensitivity (e.g., code-completion vs. chat). The fidelity latch concept is an automated, cohort-aware gate that uses simulated delta distributions to set safe rollout budgets and generate alerts/auto-rollbacks.
goals: Implement a compressed-weight simulation engine that perturbs base fp16 weights with quantization noise models (per-layer, per-bit) to approximate int8/int4 AWQ and GPTQ effects
Produce cohort-level delta distributions across representative eval suites (semantic-sim, nll, rouge/bleu proxies) within 30 minutes per profile on a 4-core CPU job
Design and validate an adaptive fidelity latch algorithm that computes per-cohort thresholds and recommended rollout budgets (canary sizes, max tokens at quantized profile)
Integrate signals into nightly evals and Redwood Console dashboards and wire alerts to the release pipeline for automatic mitigation
datasets: prod-sampled-prompts-2025-01 (10k stratified by route and token-length)
metrics: response_regression_rate (percent of samples with semantic drop beyond cohort threshold)
failure_rate (model runtime errors during simulated rollout)
approach: Phase A: Implement weight-perturbation simulator library that accepts a fp16 checkpoint and returns logits with AWQ/GPTQ-style noise applied per-layer. No kernel changes or GPU compilation required.
Phase B: Build an orchestration job (K8s batch) that runs multiple simulated profiles in parallel, aggregates per-cohort deltas, and produces a report and a threshold recommendation JSON.

Phase C: Implement adaptive fidelity latch: algorithm computes threshold = baseline_mean - alpha * baseline_std where alpha is tuned per-cohort; tune alpha to meet target false-positive/false-negative budget.
Phase D: Wire reports to Console, create 'quant-sim' nightly job, and hook the latch into rollout tooling as optional automatic gate with email/PagerDuty notifications on violation.
experiment_steps: 1) Prototype simulator in Python using additive quantization noise derived from AWQ/GPTQ calibration stats (target: < 1 hour end-to-end for 3 profiles on 4 cores)
2) Validate simulator by comparing deltas from full-compile runs on a held-out small model (gpt-small) and compute correlation (target rho >= 0.85 for semantic_similarity_delta)
3) Run full sweep across 3 model families (base-llm-A, base-llm-B, base-embed-C) and profiles (int8-AWQ, int8-GPTQ, int4-AWQ) on stratified cohorts
4) Fit alpha per-cohort using grid search to meet acceptance criteria in >90% of routes, produce recommended rollout budgets
5) Deploy latch in shadow mode for one week, surface alerts in Console, and compare with manual full runs
6) If shadow metrics match target, enable latch for canary rollouts with auto-hold and an on-call pager rule
acceptance_criteria: Simulator correlates with full-compile deltas: Spearman rho >= 0.85 on semantic_similarity_delta across test models
Nightly simulation job completes for target dataset within 30 minutes and uses <= 4 CPU cores and 8GB RAM per profile
Adaptive fidelity latch recommendations produce no more than 1% extra false rejections (blocking safe profiles) when compared to manual tuning on pilot routes
Shadow mode shows <= 2% discrepancy between simulated recommended rollback rate and full-run rollback signals over a 7-day window
Automated alerts and Console panels created and linked from rollout pages; runbook added to Confluence
rollout_plan: Week 0: Internal engineering-only run (shadow) on non-production dataset
Week 1: Shadow mode against one low-impact customer cohort (internal feature flags)
Week 2: Canary gating enabled for 5% traffic on 3 tolerant routes with auto-hold but no auto-rollback
Week 3: If canary behaves, enable auto-hold + on-call notification for additional routes; manual review required for auto-rollback
Post-rollout: daily monitoring for 14 days and then weekly
monitoring_and_alerting: Nightly run status (success/failure) - alert to #infra-ops on failures
Per-cohort semantic_similarity_delta histograms in Console with overlayed threshold and observed drift
PagerDuty rule for fidelity_latch_violation when >1% of samples in a canary exceed threshold
Slack notifications to #quant-evals with summary CSV and link to report
Automated PR generation when a profile's recommended budget changes by >25% vs currently deployed
automation_tasks: Create k8s batch job template and Helm chart for quant-sim nightly runs
Add simulator to eval-harness repo (unit tests + perf microbench)
Auto-PR bot: ingest recommended thresholds and open a PR to deployment-configs with summary and diff
Dashboard panels + alert rules in Grafana/Console
Add a smoke-checker that runs full-compile on a tiny subset if simulator recommends a large change (>40% budget shift)
risks_and_mitigation: Simulator miscalibration: mitigate by maintaining a small weekly full-compile calibration matrix and automatic recalibration if correlation drops below 0.8
Cohort drift over time: mitigate with rolling window estimation and higher alpha for low-sample cohorts
Operational noise (flaky runs): add retries and job-level checksums to ensure reproducible inputs
